name: personal-skills
description: A repo-agnostic workflow-and-design library for Claude Code, built around one front door. /orchestrate ensures a corpus/ workspace exists, reads corpus/routing.md, classifies the request and routes it — capture to corpus-flow (an LLM-maintained project wiki, glossary and decisions log plus a todos-to-briefs-to-done lifecycle), build to plan-split-dispatch (model-routed subagent implementation with a mandatory review gate, a bounded escalating fix loop and a ruling ledger that survives compaction), "what should we work on" to improve (a read-only senior-advisor survey that audits with parallel per-lens finders, vets every finding against the source and the corpus's locked decisions, ranks by leverage and writes the promoted ones up as briefs), redesigns to hallmark called by name, and questions to the wiki. Research and audit are gated: they surface options and stop for your pick, never an auto-build. grill-me interviews you in dependency-ordered rounds, finds facts itself instead of asking, and records the durable outcomes as glossary terms and decisions. On the design side it ships hallmark (the MIT design skill every web UI's redesign uses: a Floor of 16 rules no page ships without, a tiered browser lint, themes dealt per page and an index of credited Wikimedia photographs; redesign and audit by path), impeccable (the Apache-2.0 build engine, 23 sub-commands), the taste suite, run only when called by name (design-taste-frontend plus the minimalist, industrial-brutalist and high-end presets), design-md-library (74 real-brand DESIGN.md references, plus palettes and type dealt by trade and a copy layer), diagram-design (39 editorial diagram types as self-contained HTML+SVG), and web-design-guidelines / writing-guidelines wrappers that fetch Vercel's rules fresh at review time. Plus house-style (the estate's TypeScript style as numbered rules, each with its lint rule or review, and how a repo adopts the harness that checks it) with two hooks: the repo's own Prettier formats each saved file, and the repo's check:fast runs before Claude ends a turn. Plus base-ui (React UI on Base UI 1.9.0 styled with Tailwind 4, as numbered rules with the checker or review that enforces each, copy-ready wrappers compiled against the 1.9.0 types, the Light / Dark / System theme switch, and the method for moving an app from plain CSS to Tailwind). Plus code-structure (one code structure for the Fastify 5 servers and the React apps beside them, as numbered rules with the checker, the dependency-cruiser rule or the review that enforces each, copy-ready skeletons compiled and tested against Fastify 5.12 with the zod type provider, and the order every server's migration follows). Plus unslop (cut AI tells from prose), thermo-nuclear-review (an extremely strict maintainability pass), codegraph (graph-first, grep-verified code understanding), corpus-docs-site (a Docusaurus docs site generated from the corpus and the TypeScript, with a verified recipe for migrating a Starlight one), readme-docs (one README + docs/ standard with real screenshots and GIFs), ui-test-plans and bootstrap-vps-deploy. The Vercel suite adds UI and prose guideline reviews (rules fetched fresh each run), React best-practices, view transitions, and composition patterns. corpus-flow's domain-modeling layer (§9) keeps the project's vocabulary honest: an opinionated glossary where each term lists the synonyms it displaces, a decisions format with the categories that qualify, a glossary map for multi-context monorepos, and the active discipline of challenging conflicting terms and cross-referencing them against the code. See ATTRIBUTION.md.
